question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout after the branch is refreshed?
rationale: Disabling existing opt-ins and adding a Google Play Data Safety upload lane are privacy, upgrade, and release-operation choices that automation should not decide, even though the patch shape is focused.

options.title: Accept reset and rollout
options.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh conflicts, and land the PR.

options.title: Revise disclosure first
options.body: Request wording, placement, consent-version, or release-lane changes before repeating emulator and release-lane proof.

options.title: Hold for release materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until external Play Console, privacy-policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept reset and rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh conflicts, and land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily release inclusion and rollout policy, and Peter has the strongest recent release-path history among the routed candidates.
